clue.text: How backer makes down-payment, paradoxically

parts.note: a financial backer provides funds by raising them, so a payment 'down' is made by putting something up

explanation.definitionFit: To provide the funding for a venture is idiomatically to raise the cash for it, which is what a backer does.

clue.text: Conveyance of artist's in variety about noon

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the abbreviation for noon
being in variety means the letters of the painter appear in a varied, mixed-up order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letters: artist's means artist is

explanation.surface: An artist travelling between music-hall venues on the noon conveyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in variety' scrambles ARTIST into TRASIT, and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of people or goods from place to place, a form of conveyance.

clue.text: Worn out in house demolition

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of the words house demolition

explanation.surface: Someone feels exhausted by having their home knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'house' and the start of 'demolition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used is second-hand and worn, past its best.

clue.text: Enough money for one with second thoughts?

definitions.text: Enough money for one with second thoughts?

parts.words: Enough money for one with second thoughts?
parts.note: plays on 'a penny for your thoughts': a second set of thoughts would cost double that sum

explanation.definitionFit: If one set of thoughts is worth a penny, a further set costs double, a coin sum worth two of them.

clue.text: Formerly, space put up for ponies' grazing-land

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means formerly, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the word for space is written bottom to top

parts.note: room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: Somewhere that once hosted ponies has been erected again for grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ROOM into MOOR in this down light. EXMOOR is a moorland national park in south-west England, famous for its native wild ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: This upland moor in Somerset and Devon is home to a hardy native breed of wild pony that grazes there.

clue.text: He won't catch one out in a silly position

definitions.text: He won't catch one out in a silly position

parts.words: He won't catch one out in a silly position
parts.note: in cricket 'silly' positions are fielding spots very close to the batsman, so a fielder far from the bat is never in one

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, silly point and silly mid-on are fielding places almost beside the batsman; a player stationed near the boundary is never there, though he may well take catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder posted far from the bat, near the boundary, rather than close in.

clue.text: To save up, I have gone short to become deceitful

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word save is written bottom to top

parts.note: the word save is taken as written, the to being a lead-in
shortened, I have becomes the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone has had to scrimp, cutting back, and turned dishonest as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAVE into EVAS; 'I have' cut short is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being evasive means dodging the truth, so it is a form of deceit.

clue.text: Underground group needs it to change

parts.note: a clan is a family group

indicators.note: the letters of needs it are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An underground cell must have something altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges NEEDS IT into DESTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine activity is secret, like a resistance movement working underground.

clue.text: Lots of people get knocked down in it

definitions.text: Lots of people get knocked down in it

parts.words: Lots of people get knocked down in it
parts.note: at an auction, lots are sold, or knocked down, by the fall of the hammer; it reads as a scene of many people being felled

explanation.definitionFit: A room where goods are auctioned, each lot knocked down to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Sort of square lines of shadow?

parts.note: a T-square is a kind of drawing square, giving T
rails are railway lines

explanation.surface: A question about the outline of shadows forming a square.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them closely, as a detective shadows a suspect.

clue.text: First, for example, to make remarks about portion

indicators.note: the word for making remarks goes about, around, the word for portion

parts.note: to comment is to make remarks
a part is a portion

explanation.surface: Someone comments on a share of something, starting with an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is a first-class railway carriage section, of which it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-class section of a train is one example of a railway carriage division.

clue.text: French bird loses gold tail in river

indicators.note: loses signals that letters are dropped from the French word
tail says the gold letters are lost from the tail end of the French word

parts.note: oiseau is the French word for bird
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A French bird in a river sheds its golden tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' and 'tail' drop AU from the end of OISEAU. The OISE is a river in northern France, a tributary of the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oise is a French waterway that flows into the Seine near Paris.

clue.text: Sworn statement of how things were at Camptown?

definitions.meaning: a written statement made under oath, used as evidence in court
the minstrel song Camptown Races uses 'de' for 'the', so 'the position' becomes the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Camptown Races, the Stephen Foster song ('De Camptown ladies sing dis song'), renders 'the' as 'de'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal testimony given under oath, and in song dialect 'the state of affairs'.

clue.text: Beard-elite variety that is planned

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A breed of bearded elite that has been purposely designed.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is intentional, done on purpose.

clue.text: Composure of Bunthorne's bride, we hear

definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta is subtitled Bunthorne's Bride, a title we hear performed

explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of 1881 has the full title '..., or Bunthorne's Bride'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm endurance, and the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta whose subtitle is Bunthorne's Bride.

clue.text: One of twin record-holders in Cardigan

definitions.text: One of twin record-holders in Cardigan

parts.words: One of twin record-holders in Cardigan
parts.note: a cardigan has two arm coverings, and a vinyl record is kept in a cardboard cover; Cardigan also looks like the Welsh town

explanation.definitionFit: The arm of a knitted cardigan, of which there are two, and the cover in which a vinyl disc is stored.

clue.text: Blue players depressed

parts.note: feeling down means feeling depressed
the cast are the players in a production

explanation.surface: Actors of a sad play are feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means being sad and dejected.

clue.text: Dried fruit is engulfed by water

indicators.note: one word is engulfed by, swallowed inside, another

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Dried fruit becomes swamped in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar dried fruit.

clue.text: One who makes a cover-charge

parts.note: reads like a restaurant's cover charge, but means someone charging premiums for insurance cover

explanation.definitionFit: A company providing cover against risk charges premiums for that protection.

clue.text: Bedspread to disguise rent?

parts.note: to cover something up is to disguise it
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A bedspread used to hide a tear in the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a light quilt laid over a bed.

clue.text: Battle of the French show

parts.note: le is French for the
a panto is a pantomime, a Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: A French-themed battle-scene staged as a show.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is a British Christmas family stage show. LEPANTO was the 1571 naval battle where a Holy League fleet defeated the Ottomans.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval engagement of 1571 off Greece in which Christian forces beat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: These days, exchange percentage is very slow

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
agio is the percentage charged for exchanging currency

explanation.surface: Currency exchange fees are moving at a crawl nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the tempo marking means at a leisurely pace, slower than andante.

clue.text: Single maid turns out deceitful

indicators.note: the letters turn out, emerging in a fresh order

explanation.definitionFit: Something misleading gives a false impression, so it deceives.

clue.text: Brisk drive, second to the flag

parts.note: in golf the pin is the flagstick on the green

explanation.surface: A quick drive in a golf round, coming second to the flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure ride in a car.

clue.text: Enough land for medley-race?

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of race are mixed

explanation.surface: Is there enough land to hold a swimming medley relay?
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Girl from manor, perhaps…

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A young woman from the country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's name.

clue.text: … girl starting school is taking brief looks

indicators.note: the starting letter of girl is taken

parts.note: Lancing College is an English public school in Sussex

explanation.surface: A girl beginning at a school keeps peeking.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING is a well-known boarding school in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look briefly, so glancing means giving quick looks.

clue.text: Wellington's discharge?

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington gave his name to the rubber wellington, so his dismissal fancifully involves footwear

explanation.walkthrough: A wellington is a rubber boot named after the Duke; getting this is a jocular phrase for being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular phrase for dismissal from a job, as if honoured with a decoration.
